questions.knowledge_point: Solving for a Variable in a Singular Matrix
questions.problem: If $F=[\begin{aligned}3 & t \\ t & 3\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value(s) of $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $F$ is singular if and only if $det(F)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(F) & =3\cdot 3-t\cdot t \\  & =9-{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9-{t}^{2} & =0 \\ {t}^{2} & =9 \\ t & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the values of $t$ are $t=\pm 3.$

questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
N=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,Z=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- For the matrix $N$, we have

$$
det(N)=3\cdot 0-0\cdot 1=0.
$$

Because $det(N)=0,$ we conclude that $N$ is not invertible. Since $N$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $N$ is singular.

- The matrix $V$ is a $5\times 1$ matrix. So, it is not invertible. Since the matrix is not square, we can't say that it's singular.

- For the matrix $Z$, we have

$$
det(Z)=0\cdot 0-2\cdot 8=-16.
$$

Because $det(Z)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $Z$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $N$ is singular.

questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
S=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 4 & -6\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- For the matrix $S$, we have

$$
det(S)=1\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot 0=-1.
$$

Because $det(S)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $S$ is invertible.

- For the matrix $T$, we have

$$
det(T)=2\cdot (-6)-4\cdot (-3)=0.
$$

Because $det(T)=0,$ we conclude that $T$ is not invertible. Since $T$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $T$ is singular.

- For the matrix $U$, we have

$$
det(U)=0\cdot 0-1\cdot (-1)=1.
$$

Because $det(U)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $U$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $T$ is singular.

questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below does **not** have an inverse?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 15 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- The matrix $A$ is a $3\times 1$ matrix. So, it is not invertible.

- For the matrix $B$, we have

$$
det(B)=-3\cdot 5-1\cdot 15=-30.
$$

Because $det(B)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $B$ is invertible.

- For the matrix $C$, we have

$$
det(C)=7\cdot 2-3\cdot 4=2.
$$

Because $det(C)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $C$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $A$ does not have an inverse.

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for a Variable in a Singular Matrix
questions.problem:
Let $B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -x+7 \\ x-5 & 0\end{aligned}]$
be a singular matrix. **In ascending order**, the values of $x$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}}$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $B$ is singular if and only if $det(B)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =3\cdot 0-(-x+7)\cdot (x-5) \\  & ={x}^{2}-5x-7x+35 \\  & ={x}^{2}-12x+35.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-12x+35 & =0 \\ (x-7)(x-5) & =0 \\ x & =7,5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the values of $x$ are

$$
x=5\,\text{and}\,x=7.
$$
